editorial_reason: ProofWiki Definition:Martingale/Discrete Time separately states the one-step and all-later-time criteria. The two formulations are equivalent by conditional-expectation tower property and adaptedness with integrability; that equivalence is separately presented as a theorem. Equality is almost sure, not pointwise. This meaning is scoped to real-valued integrable adapted sequences and integer time, not continuous-index processes or local martingales. Both formulations go under the same contextual meaning.

The verified ProofWiki Martingale page explicitly distinguishes continuous-time filtration indexing from discrete-time indexing and states integrability and conditional expectations for any ordered times. The term continuous-time refers only to the index set, not to continuous trajectories: almost-sure continuous sample paths are a strictly stronger optional regularity condition. The s=t case follows from adaptedness and integrability. Preserve the alternate mathematical context under the same displayed term grouping.

ProofWiki's direct Definition:Chromatic Number states the minimum positive integer k admitting a proper vertex k-coloring. The independently authored formulation specifies finite, loopless, nonempty simple undirected graphs to avoid distinct empty graph and loop conventions and clarifies palette semantics: a coloring may use fewer than k labels. It does not concern edge chromatic number or total chromatic number. MathWorld separately supports the positive chromatic polynomial alternative, but it remains held until a distinct source-registration/rights review permits that observation.
